concepts.gag_line: The show goes on, at 3am, to an auditorium of empty seats and one raised hand.
concepts.metaphor: The committee sitting as a theatre performance: the cancellation notice is the sign on the box office door, and the vote is the show playing to nobody.

caricature_handles: reading glasses pushed up into her hair
cast.role_in_frame: Centre stage, mid-address, one hand raised in a vote

concepts.composition: Wide shot from the rear stalls. Rows of empty red seats fill the foreground; the lit stage is small and distant. A clock above the proscenium reads 03:00. A hand-lettered plate hangs on the door at frame left.
read_order: the single lit figure with a raised hand

lettering_plan.placement: hand-lettered plate on the door at frame left

concepts.gag_line: Dinner was cancelled, so she ate the whole thing herself.
concepts.metaphor: The budget as a family meal: a note on the fridge cancels dinner while one diner works through every plate at the table alone.

caricature_handles: reading glasses pushed up into her hair
dark blazer worn over an apron
cast.role_in_frame: Seated alone at a long table, mid-meal

concepts.composition: Long dining table shot down its length, five empty place settings and one occupied. A kitchen clock at the rear reads 03:00. A note is stuck to the fridge behind her.
read_order: the long table of empty settings

lettering_plan.placement: note on the fridge door, rear of frame

concepts.gag_line: The out-of-order machine dispenses anyway, to nobody, at three in the morning.
concepts.metaphor: The committee as a vending machine bearing an out-of-order sign, quietly dispensing a sack of money into an empty corridor.

caricature_handles: reading glasses pushed up into her hair
hand withdrawing from the machine's side panel
cast.role_in_frame: Half-visible at frame edge, walking away

concepts.composition: A dim corridor at night, single overhead strip light. The machine dominates centre frame with a taped sign on its glass; a sack drops into the tray. A figure exits at frame right.
read_order: the taped sign on the machine
the sack dropping into the tray

lettering_plan.placement: taped sign across the machine's glass front

candidates.critique: The theatre concept wins on read order: the empty seats land before anything else and carry the whole point, so the drawing works even at column width on a phone screen. The machine concept is sharper but reads as an accusation of deliberate self-dealing, which is exactly the motive claim S6 stripped as unverified — it implies what we cannot assert. The strongest objection to the theatre concept is that the empty-auditorium device is a well-worn editorial trope and an alert reader may find it familiar; it survives because the 03:00 clock and the cancellation plate make it specific to this story rather than generic.

concepts.gag_line: The new housing plan, fresh off the photocopier, still warm from 2019.
concepts.metaphor: Policy recycling made literal: the minister unveils a presentation board that is visibly a photocopy, the machine still running behind him.

cast.figure: Avner Gilad, Minister of Transport and Housing
cast.role_in_frame: At the podium, gesturing proudly at the board

concepts.composition: Press-conference three-quarter view. Minister at frame left at a podium; an easel board at frame right showing an architectural rendering with visible copier streaks and a curled corner. Behind him a photocopier mid-cycle, identical sheets stacking into the tray.
read_order: the dated corner of the page

lettering_plan.placement: banner across the top of the easel board

concepts.gag_line: Tonight's special: yesterday's, reheated and replated.
concepts.metaphor: The announcement as a restaurant dish — a waiter presents a domed silver platter which, uncovered, holds an obviously reheated portion with a 2019 date label still on the wrap.

cast.figure: Avner Gilad, Minister of Transport and Housing
caricature_handles: waiter's folded cloth over the forearm
cast.role_in_frame: Presenting the platter with a flourish

concepts.composition: Tight two-thirds frame on the platter being uncovered at a table, minister behind it. The cling film and its date label are the sharpest-focus element in the picture.
read_order: the flourish of the platter lid
the cling film still on the food

concepts.gag_line: Same backdrop, new announcement — the stagehands did not even change the scenery.
concepts.metaphor: A painted theatrical backdrop of a housing development being lowered into place for the second time, its reverse side stencilled with the year it was first used.

cast.figure: Avner Gilad, Minister of Transport and Housing
cast.role_in_frame: Downstage, arms wide, presenting the backdrop

concepts.composition: Side-on stage view so both faces of the descending backdrop are visible: painted housing towers facing the audience, stencilled year facing the wings.
read_order: the stencilled year on its reverse

lettering_plan.placement: stencilled on the reverse of the backdrop, visible from the wings

candidates.critique: The photocopier concept is the most legible thing on the whole slate — copier streaks and a stacking tray are universally understood and need no caption. The backdrop concept is the most elegant but demands the reader parse a side-on stage view to find the joke on the reverse face, which is a fourth-position read and therefore a failure. The strongest objection to the copier concept is that it is the obvious idea, the one any cartoonist would reach for first; it is chosen anyway because obviousness is a virtue in a single frame read in eight seconds over breakfast.
